Meanwhile modern systems lean on caching to hide slow disk reads. A well-tuned cache sits between the app and storage, holding hot rows in memory. Latency drops sharply, and the database survives traffic spikes that would otherwise crush it entirely.

However a cache adds risk; stale data is the classic hazard. Writes must invalidate keys, or readers see ghosts of old rows. Teams pick policies carefully: write-through keeps the cache fresh but costs latency; write-behind is faster yet loses data during crashes. Sizing matters too, since a tiny cache thrashes and returns almost constant misses.

Along traffic paths, that fast RAM pool absorbs bulk load; without it, a big SQL farm grinds against disk again and again, burning capacity until timing counts drop off. Hot data stays put, so most apps gain a solid win.

Finally measure everything: hit ratios, eviction rates, and cache lag. Tune slowly, verify results, and then your work is done.
